call_points.text: Long-run gross margin guidance stays at about 32%, with no predictability on inflation.
call_points.versus_prior: narrowed from 32-34% in the July call to about 32%

call_points.text: Double-digit EBITDA margin expected in the next four to six quarters, at least in H2 onwards.
Revenue growth guidance of more than 15% CAGR, slightly more aggressive than earlier.
Price hikes cover 80-100% of inflation depending on category; fans about 80%, appliances about 90%, wires close to 100%.
Working capital at 34 days, targeted to return to about 20 days in four to six quarters.
call_points.versus_prior: up from 25 days cited in the July call

call_points.text: Wires more than doubled YoY but launched only in North, East and parts of South, not pan-India.
Analyst pressed on the 250 bps gross margin drop despite price hikes; management said inflation outpaced price increases.
Management aims for 32-34% gross margin on a BAU basis, but guidance is difficult due to volatile commodity inflation.
EBITDA margin improvement trajectory continues, with focus on cost prudence and productivity gains from Project Sanchay.
Strong seasonal recovery with no inventory buildup; primary and secondary sales were balanced, driven by volume growth.
Fixed cost investments were made ahead of the curve; future spending will be on growth requirements, not cuts.
Net cash position of ₹133 Cr and working capital days at 25 days reflect strong balance sheet discipline.
Lighting and Switchgear delivered 16% YoY revenue growth driven by distribution expansion and premiumization.
Project Sanchay generated ₹68 crores of cost savings during FY26, supporting margin resilience.
The company implemented calibrated price increases of over 6% in fans and lighting entering Q1 FY27 to counter commodity inflation.
BLDC fans portfolio grew over 50% YoY and now contributes 25% of domestic ceiling fans revenue.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: In respect to GST demand (DRC-01A) received under Section 74(5) and as intimated to stock exchange on June 29, 2024. The company had received Order in original in under Section 74(9) confirming the liability amount in respect of the following matter. a. Import of goods at a higher rate of GST and further supply at the correct lower rate of GST: The department has confirmed the demand of Rs. 19,68,20,508/- on the supplies made by the company and penalty of Rs 19,68,20,508/- and interest thereon. b. Payment of GST on moulds supplied on free of cost basis by company to supplier: Department has confirmed the GST demand of Rs. 63,87,402 and penalty of Rs 63,87,402/- and interest thereon. Company has filled writ petition with Hon’ble High court of Maharashtra on May 06, 2025.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Joint Commissioner of (Anti Evasion) CGST and Excise, Thane (Maharashtra)
tax_litigation.status: No change in status. Writ petition filed with Hon’ble High court of Maharashtra. The matter was not heard on last date i.e 04-03-2026. Next date of hearing is yet to be updated.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Import of goods at a higher rate of GST and further supply at the correct lower rate of GST: The company had imported goods falling under Entry no. 438A and paid IGST at the higher rate of 18% and availed credit of the same. The said goods have been supplied by the Company to its customers by classifying it under the heading under entry number 226 and 227 of Schedule II of Notification No. 01/2017 CT (Rate) dated 28.06.2017 and paid GST @12% instead of 18%. Accordingly, the department has raised the differential demand of Tax of Rs. 6,70,615/, penalty amounting to Rs. 6,70,615/- and applicable interest on tax demand. Company has filled appeal against the said demand order with Appellate Authority.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Superintendent of Central Tax Ibrahimpatnam CGST Range (Andhra Pradesh)
tax_litigation.status: No change in status. Appeal is yet to be listed for hearing.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Demand against the differential GST on supply of Goods. The company had imported goods falling under Entry no. 438A and paid IGST at the higher rate of 18% and availed credit of the same. The said goods have been supplied by the Company to its depot at Madhya Pradesh and further sold to customers by classifying it under the heading under entry number 226 and 227 of Schedule 11 of Notification No. 01/2017 CT (Rate) dated 28.06.2017 and paid GST @12% instead of 18%. Accordingly, the department has raised demand for the differential amount of Rs. 8,86,47,756/- and penalty Rs. 8,86,47,756/- and interest on demand on the supplies made by the company. Company has filled writ petition with Hon’ble High court of Madhya Pradesh on April 24, 2025.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Joint Commissioner, C.G.S.T and Central Excise Commissionerate. Indore
tax_litigation.status: No change in status Matter is under hearing with MP high court. Next date of hearing is yet to be updated.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company has received the demand order from Assistant Commissioner, Commercial Taxes Department, Tamil Nadu (Egmore, North-III, Chennai North),(Demand of INR 51,59,48,406/-) wherein major demand pertains to the alleged non-reversal of input tax credit on inter-unit balances remaining unpaid after 180 days. Further, demand is also raised on non-reversal of input tax credit on credit notes received from vendors, ineligible ITC and outstanding trade payables balance remaining unpaid after 180 days. Based on assessment of facts the Company and advice of legal expert, Company is of the view that the levy of GST demand along with interest and penalty is without considering submissions made, facts of our case and hence it is without merit, unjustified and unsustainable in law.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Assistant Commissioner, Commercial Taxes Department, Tamil Nadu (Egmore, North-III, Chennai North)
tax_litigation.status: No change in status as compared to Dec -25. The same has been paid and closed.

industry: Consumer Discretionary > Consumer Durables > Household Appliances

operating_notes.text: FY26 raw material cost fell 5.0% to ₹851.73 Cr while revenue rose 7.5% to ₹3,326.39 Cr.
Trade receivables rose to ₹621.29 Cr at Mar-2026 from ₹517.78 Cr a year earlier, absorbing ₹121.59 Cr of cash.
GST: Kerala (₹4.48 Cr) and Jammu (₹0.22 Cr) show cause notices dropped with nil demand; Andhra Pradesh demand of ₹5.74 Cr confirmed; ₹64.31 Cr of demand orders under appeal.
Q4FY26 standalone revenue grew 10% YoY to ₹948.3 Cr and PAT grew 28.9% YoY to ₹40.3 Cr.
Project Sanchay delivered ₹68 crores of cost savings during FY26.
Project Sanchay delivered ₹10 Cr cost savings in Q1FY27.
DTM network added ~3,600 new retailers in Q1FY27.
BLDC fans now constitute 27-30% of ceiling fan revenue.
Electrical consumer durables revenue was ₹550.50 Cr in Q2FY27 versus ₹440.91 Cr a year ago, and Lighting & switchgear ₹328.84 Cr versus ₹261.70 Cr.
H1FY27 inventories absorbed ₹92.12 Cr of cash, leaving operating cash flow at ₹7.78 Cr against EBITDA of ₹123.39 Cr.
A ₹3.96 Cr exceptional write-down of Noida plant assets to net realisable value was booked in Q1FY27 following board approval to consolidate manufacturing facilities at Noida.
BLDC fan portfolio grew 26% in Q2FY27, with management citing innovation-led launches in BLDC fans and consumer lighting.
Distribution reaches 1,35,000 retail outlets and a service network covering more than 450 cities.
BLDC fans grew 26% YoY and are about 30% of ceiling fans, versus industry at 17-18%.
Hyderabad plant at about 40% utilisation on a single shift, producing 75% PPW and 20-25% ceiling fans.
Wires more than doubled YoY but launched only in North, East and parts of South, not pan-India.
